claims.text: Argo CD compares the manifests at the Application's target revision with the live objects; sync status is Synced when they match and OutOfSync when any object differs or is missing.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Core Concepts (Sync status, Live state, Target state); User Guide > Sync Status; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.txt

claims.text: A sync applies the manifests at the target revision to the cluster, in the manner of kubectl apply, so the live objects match Git.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Core Concepts (Sync); FAQ / Sync Options (Argo CD uses kubectl apply by default)

claims.text: The sync policy (spec.syncPolicy) is what lets Argo CD start syncs by itself; an Application with none (staging-manual.yaml) reports OutOfSync and waits until someone starts a sync.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy (manual sync by default); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml:5-6

claims.text: Health status is assessed separately from sync status; built-in values include Healthy, Progressing, Degraded, Missing. A Deployment is Progressing while its rollout is not complete (new Pods not yet available) and Healthy once it is.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Resource Health (Deployment health check: rollout status)

claims.text: An Application's health is the worst health among the resources it manages, so one unhealthy Deployment keeps the Application from Healthy.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Resource Health (application health aggregates its resources; worst status wins)

claims.text: Health Missing is reported for objects that are in Git but do not exist in the cluster yet (named in Core concepts and How it works); before the first sync the Application staging is OutOfSync, Missing.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Resource Health (Missing); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.txt:3

claims.text: Argo CD looks only at manifests in the Application's path and live objects with its tracking annotation, written on each object it applies in a sync; namespace donhang (made by OpenTofu, no manifest in envs/staging) is neither: not in status.resources, not reported missing, not changed.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Resource Tracking; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.sh:51-55, outputs/.../gitops-first-sync.txt:62-63

claims.text: Argo CD rereads the repository on an interval (not at once); setting the annotation argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=normal on an Application asks it to compare now. The lesson states no interval value.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: FAQ (How often does Argo CD check for changes; timeout.reconciliation); Declarative Setup / annotations (argocd.argoproj.io/refresh); scripts/lib/gitops.sh:104-107

claims.text: Writing an operation with sync.revision into an Application via kubectl patch makes Argo CD run a sync without the argocd CLI; the result is reported in .status.operationState.phase (Succeeded in the script's run).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Application spec / status (operation, operationState); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.sh:31-38, output line 'sync: Succeeded'

claims.text: gitops-first-sync.sh@stage-3 output: OutOfSync/Missing with every resource OutOfSync; after the sync 'sync: Succeeded', staging Synced Progressing with api 0/2 ready; then Synced Healthy with api 2/2; namespace check prints no.
Argo CD does not call the api's /health/ready itself; its Deployment health reads the Deployment's status (updated/available replicas), which depends on Pods passing the readiness probe.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Resource Health (Deployment); Kubernetes docs: Deployment status, readiness probes; envs/staging/api.yaml:54-64

claims.text: The api's readiness endpoint /health/ready fails when the api cannot reach PostgreSQL, so such an api never becomes ready and the Application stays Synced but not Healthy.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 src/DonHang.Api/Program.cs (health checks, ready tag); lesson k8s.l1.readiness-probes summary line 3

claims.text: app_refresh, app_wait and the kubectl wrapper adding --context kind-donhang-staging come from scripts/lib/gitops.sh, sourced at gitops-first-sync.sh:6; app_wait's 3rd argument is a revision (empty = any), the 4th a limit in seconds.

Try it: kubectl get application staging -n argocd shows SYNC STATUS and HEALTH STATUS; before the sync OutOfSync, Missing; after gitops-first-sync.sh Synced, Healthy. The script prints the status at each point it waits for, once reached, and stays quiet in between.
